items.claim: The row's sole boundary driver types the temporal opener at Jer.50.4 as a date-formula onset, but that formula is not a member of the book's byte-classified date-header object, and the claimed recurrence at Jer.50.20 crosses two different forms.
items.evidence: MT 50:4 opens בַּיָּמִ֨ים הָהֵ֜מָּה וּבָעֵ֤ת הַהִיא֙ (oshb:Jer.50.4, byte tier) at tokens 1-4 of 20, and the row's stated warrant reads it as a date-formula onset, with the row's only substrate signal keyed to the date-frame family. The book's date-header object is built on the year-word token plus the bet-plus-cardinal shape and carries 19 classified candidate sites; neither Jer.50.4 nor Jer.50.20 stands among them, and that object already separates year-shaped material that is not a date on a per-site read. Typing an eschatological temporal opener into that family blends two separately swept objects and imports tier-1 seam weight the object does not carry at these two verses; a scene-and-addressee-shift warrant at the same seam would stand on the bytes, and the substrate-signal field is dependent on whichever driver is chosen. The recurrence claim compounds it: Jer.50.4 reads hahemah, and a skeleton sweep of its four-token opener returns that verse alone (sweep: 1 verse, verse counts, MT keys), while Jer.50.20 reads הָהֵם֩ (oshb:Jer.50.20, byte tier), hahem, whose four-token opener sweeps to two sites (sweep: 2 verses, Jer.33.15 and Jer.50.20, verse counts, MT keys). The pair is therefore not one recurring form, and the note asserts recurrence with neither the form split nor a tier label. What verifies: both spliced runs reach byte tier at their cited refs; the SAMEKH closing MT 50:5 is real (tier-3, single witness); no other mark, paseq or ketiv/qere note falls in MT 50:4-50:5, so span disclosure is complete. The declared heuristic false positive on the pairing sentence is CONFIRMED: the flagged word is a keyword match on non-exclusive prose, not a universal claim.

items.claim: Both ketiv/qere notes at Jer.50.6 are correctly located, correctly formed and correctly paired in the verse's own bytes, and the span's mark disclosure is complete.
items.evidence: MT 50:6 runs 16 whitespace tokens. The unpointed ketiv היה stands at token 3 with the pointed qere הָי֣וּ at token 4, and the unpointed ketiv שובבים at token 9 with the pointed qere שֽׁוֹבְב֑וּם at token 10 (all oshb:Jer.50.6, byte tier): exactly the pairing, order and reading direction the row states, and the ketiv/qere inventory records 2 notes there, one of the twelve multi-note sites in the book. The composite opening run quoted in the row also reaches byte tier at oshb:Jer.50.6. Mark symmetry is complete: SAMEKH at MT 50:5 immediately before the span and SAMEKH at MT 50:7 at its close (tier-3, single witness), with no paseq and no further note inside MT 50:6-50:7. Both declared heuristic false positives are CONFIRMED: the flagged words carry no exclusivity, and the statement that each ketiv's consonantal form is spliced and named beside its qere is true of both notes. Two reservations for the record, neither byte-contested. First, the note types both variants as correcting number or voice; the first pair is a number correction on the verb, but the second differs in its termination (final mem after yod against final mem after vav), and no morphology layer is staged to settle that class, so the label outruns what the bytes decide. Second, the flock token צֹ֤אן stands verse-initial at MT 50:6 and the same token צֹֽאן stands verse-final at MT 50:8 (byte tier), a lexical echo straddling this span's own back seam that no row across the run discloses; the hard SAMEKH at MT 50:7 and the turn from indictment to imperative outweigh it, and the two uses carry different referents, but it is undisclosed.

items.claim: The row places the Jer.50.8 ketiv/qere note on the verse's closing verb, but the verse's own bytes put it mid-verse, and the ketiv and qere are glossed in the quotation form the book reserves for translation text.
items.evidence: MT 50:8 runs 11 whitespace tokens: the unpointed ketiv יצאו stands at token 6 with the pointed qere צֵ֑אוּ at token 7, and the verse then continues וִהְי֕וּ כְּעַתּוּדִ֖ים לִפְנֵי צֹֽאן (oshb:Jer.50.8, byte tier) at tokens 8-11. The note therefore sits mid-verse; the last verb in the verse is וִהְי֕וּ, not the ketiv/qere word, and the verse closes on a noun phrase. The substance of the note is right, a perfect corrected to an imperative, but the position is byte-false, and a ketiv/qere verse is precisely where the notes must be read before any position or slicing claim is made. Second, the ketiv and the qere are each glossed inside curly double quotes although neither wording stands in the translation at that verse, whose own imperative clause is worded differently; the book-wide convention reserves curly doubles for translation text, and neither gloss carries a translation-side ref beside it. Third, a small extent mismatch at 50:9: the English gloss begins one word earlier than the spliced run, which opens at מֵעִיר֩ and leaves אָנֹכִ֡י (oshb:Jer.50.9, byte tier) outside it, so gloss extent and splice extent do not match. What holds: both spliced runs reach byte tier at their cited refs; the closure reading in the rejected alternative is byte-true, since the neum formula at MT 50:10 occupies tokens 7-8 of 8 and is genuinely verse-final; and no mark, no paseq and no further note falls in MT 50:8-50:10 beyond the one disclosed. The declared heuristic false positive is CONFIRMED: a keyword match on non-exclusive prose.

items.claim: The cross-reference is placed in the wrong chapter, and a refrain-family substrate signal is declared with no sweep behind it while a sweep returns three sites for the shared verb pair, not two.
items.evidence: The row calls Jer.49.17 this chapter's own Edom oracle; the row's span lies in ch 50 and the cited verse lies in ch 49, so the locational statement is wrong on the row's only cross-row evidence. The row also declares a refrain-family substrate signal while stating in the same breath that no sweep stands behind it: a skeleton sweep of the two-verb pair יִשֹּׁ֥ם וְיִשְׁרֹ֖ק returns three sites (sweep: 3 verses, Jer.19.8, Jer.49.17 and Jer.50.13; verse counts, MT keys), so the two-site framing omits Jer.19.8, while the fuller run carrying the named object and the suffixed noun returns one (sweep: 1 verse, verse counts, MT keys). Neither digit is given, and a declared recurrence object owes its swept object, its unit and a digit. What is strong and fully verified: all four ketiv/qere notes at MT 50:11 stand in the bytes in the row's own order, unpointed ketiv with pointed qere at tokens 2-3, 5-6, 10-11 and 14-15 of 16, the first pair reading תשמחי against תִשְׂמְחוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.50.11, byte tier), and the inventory records exactly 4 notes there, the densest single-verse count in this run; every spliced form in the row reaches byte tier at its cited ref. The singular-to-plural characterization stands on the consonantal terminations (yod against vav) and on the plural rendering in the translation, which is the right way to argue a form class with no morphology layer staged. The stated difference from Jer.49.17 is byte-accurate: that verse reads עָלֶ֔יהָ where MT 50:13 reads עַל בָּבֶ֔ל, and its suffixed plagues noun מַכּוֹתֶֽהָ lacks the yod carried in מַכּוֹתֶֽיהָ (byte tier at oshb:Jer.49.17 and oshb:Jer.50.13). No mark, paseq or further note falls in MT 50:11-50:13, so nothing else is owed.

items.claim: The koh-amar onset at Jer.50.18 is the only one in this whole run, it carries the full divine-title stack at the digit the row cites, and its frame owner is named inside the formula's own bytes.
items.evidence: A skeleton scan of MT 50:4-50:21 finds exactly one koh-amar site, MT 50:18, so the onset the row cuts on competes with no embedded or quoted formula anywhere in the run; the mouth is named inside the quoted formula itself as the divine title, and this chapter carries no human speaker reciting the formula, unlike the confrontation and letter material earlier in the book where a false prophet speaks the full divine formula. The opening splice לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.50.18, byte tier) matches tokens 1-7 of the verse, and a skeleton sweep of the complete title stack returns Jer.50.18 among its sites (sweep: 32 verses, verse counts, MT keys), so the digit the row cites is correct and names its object and unit. The closing splice matches tokens 1-6 of MT 50:20 at byte tier, and the row's transliteration correctly reads hahem there, keeping it distinct from the hahemah form at Jer.50.4 rather than collapsing the two. No mark, no paseq and no ketiv/qere note falls anywhere in MT 50:18-50:20; the SAMEKH at MT 50:17 before the span and the unmarked internal seam after 50:19 are both correctly reported, with absence not used as evidence in either direction. One item carried forward rather than charged against this boundary: the row repeats a date-frame substrate key for the Jer.50.20 temporal opener, which the book's classified date-header object does not contain, the same typing question raised at Jer.50.4. The boundary here rests on the koh-amar onset and the title stack, and stands without that key.

items.claim: The one-verse cut is byte-warranted at both ends: an imperative onset visible in the verse's own bytes, and the verse's single disclosure object, a SAMEKH at its close, cited correctly.
items.evidence: The splice עַל הָאָ֤רֶץ מְרָתַ֨יִם֙ עֲלֵ֣ה עָלֶ֔יהָ וְאֶל יוֹשְׁבֵ֖י פְּק֑וֹד (oshb:Jer.50.21, byte tier) matches tokens 1-8 of 17 exactly. The addressee change from the remnant promise closing MT 50:20 to a command aimed at the attacking force is visible in the imperative עֲלֵ֣ה עָלֶ֔יהָ (oshb:Jer.50.21, byte tier) itself and not only in the translation, so the substrate signal the row declares is carried by the bytes. Disclosure is complete: a SAMEKH closes MT 50:21 (tier-3, single witness), and the verse carries no paseq and no ketiv/qere note, so nothing further is owed in this span. The neum formula sits at tokens 12-13 of 17, mid-verse, which is what the row reports in describing the says-Yahweh tag, and the row correctly declines to press it as a closure signal, closure corroboration being available only where a fresh onset follows. Leaving the Merathaim and Pekod name-versus-wordplay question open is the right posture with no morphology layer staged. One reservation, not byte-contested: the quoted translation run elides two words with an ellipsis while the spliced Hebrew retains עֲלֵ֣ה עָלֶ֔יהָ, so the Hebrew extent exceeds the English extent; the quoted wording is otherwise verbatim.
